stem: Each function below models an amount \(Q(t)\) of a substance \(t\) years after it was first measured. Which function models an amount that decreases by \(30\%\) each year?
solution: A decrease of \(30\%\) each year keeps \(100\% - 30\% = 70\%\) of the amount each year.
So the amount is multiplied by \(0.7\) each year: \(Q(t) = 500(0.7)^{t}\).

explanation.A: Correct. Multiplying by \(0.7\) each year keeps \(70\%\), a decrease of \(30\%\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. A base of \(0.3\) keeps only \(30\%\) each year, a decrease of \(70\%\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. A base of \(1.3\) models an increase of \(30\%\) each year.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This linear function decreases by a fixed 0.3 unit each year, not by a percent.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'D': 'A', 'A': 'B', 'B': 'C', 'C': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'D', 'B': 'A', 'C': 'B', 'D': 'C'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
t = symbols('t')
ok = [k for k in choices if simplify(value(choices[k].split('=')[1]).subs(t, 1) / value(choices[k].split('=')[1]).subs(t, 0) - Rational(7, 10)) == 0 and simplify(value(choices[k].split('=')[1]).subs(t, 2) / value(choices[k].split('=')[1]).subs(t, 1) - Rational(7, 10)) == 0]
assert ok == [answer]
